lesson_title: Finance and Data Practice Run at Examination Pace
hook_text: The mark allocation is an instruction. Most people never read it.
clip_script: A 150-mark practice paper, Mathematical Literacy — and the mark allocations are doing all the talking. Question One: thirty marks of single-step credit — VAT on R180 is R27, net pay is gross minus deductions, done. That's your warm-up lap, banked. Question Two, Finance — and here's the electricity tariff that catches thousands. First 100 units at R1,80, the next block R2,40, the top block R3,10. The house used 460. Do NOT charge all 460 at the top rate — the tariff is a staircase. 100 times 1,80 is 180, then 300 times 2,40 is 720, then 60 times 3,10 is 186. Subtotal 1 086, times 1,15 for VAT: R1 248,90. Six marks, one per stair. Now the secret the marking plan keeps: follow-through. Slip on one stair? Carry your wrong number forward and keep the operations clean — every later step still pays. An abandoned question pays nothing, ever. And read the mark allocation like an instruction: two marks, one line. Six marks, show the staircase. Comment questions? A sentence with a computed number inside it — the mean is 59 BUT a quarter of the group sits below 49. Numbers plus because equals marks. Walk a full practice paper once at exam pace and the real thing becomes your second rehearsal.
visual_style: A practice paper unfolding into a floor-plan-style map of five questions; an electricity tariff drawn as a literal staircase with rand amounts stacking per step; a red slip mark flowing forward through green ticks; a mark-allocation dial translating (2), (4), (6) into line counts.
pacing: Fast opening map, deliberate slow-down on the staircase tariff, punchy follow-through reveal, quick-fire closing habits.
call_to_action: Watch the full practice run and sit your finals like it's your third time seeing them.
